description: Patch releases are automerged here, on the strength of what the Molecule suite checks and what Ghostfolio's patch releases have actually contained.

The thing that argues against it is real and worth stating first: the ghostfolio/ghostfolio entrypoint runs `npx prisma migrate deploy` followed by `npx prisma db seed` on every single start, forward-only, before `node main` is executed at all - a fresh 3.54.0 applies 119 migrations that way - and the database it rewrites holds the users' accounts, activities and account balances. An automerged bump that carried a migration would therefore alter that schema unattended, with no way back short of restoring a backup.

Patch releases do not carry migrations. Every bump this preset can actually take is an X.Y.Z -> X.Y.Z+1 within the same minor, and in the whole 3.x line that is four of them: 3.0.0 -> 3.0.1, 3.15.0 -> 3.15.1, 3.19.0 -> 3.19.1 and 3.48.0 -> 3.48.1. None of the four touches prisma/ at all; they are UI and API bugfixes (3.48.1 is the widest at 44 files, and is a controller refactor with no schema change). Five patch versions exist across roughly sixty-five releases, so this is a rare and deliberately small kind of release upstream.

3.59.1 is not a counter-example even though it did add a migration. There is no 3.59.0 - neither as a git tag nor as a container tag - so Renovate reads 3.58.0 -> 3.59.1 as a minor bump, and minor and major bumps still require review. That is where a migration or a behavior change realistically arrives here, and it is where a human still looks.

What earns the automerge is that a branch only merges once Molecule is green on it, on Ubuntu 26.04 and Debian 13. That suite creates the instance's first user over the API and authenticates as it, reads the version back from two independent leaves (the /api/v1/admin endpoint and the package manifest of the bundle node is running), writes an account over the API and finds that row in the Postgres container at the other end of the bind-mounted Unix socket, counts the migrations Prisma recorded there, and makes Ghostfolio cache a portfolio snapshot under the new user's id in the Valkey container. It also proves that its own health check means something: /api/v1/healthz is a 404 while any path under a locale prefix is a 200 with the single-page application shell, so a status code alone would have proven nothing.

The residual risk this leaves is an upgrade-only migration failure: Molecule installs onto an empty database, so a migration that succeeds on a fresh schema and fails on a populated one would not be caught. That is the price of the automerge, and it is bounded by patch releases not shipping migrations in the first place.
The `regex` schedule below is kept: branches for the managed version open on Mondays only, so an automerged patch lands on a known day rather than whenever upstream publishes.

On the annotation in defaults/main.yml: `versioning=semver` is load-bearing. ghostfolio/ghostfolio publishes floating `2`, `3` and `latest` tags, none of which are valid semver versions, so under `semver` they drop out as candidates; the `-alpha` and `-beta.N` tags are valid semver prereleases and are skipped as unstable. Only the plain X.Y.Z tags remain, which is the intent. No `extractVersion` is needed, as the tags carry no flavour suffix.
